answer: A marketplace can require every agent to post a refundable bond before it may bid, with bids capped in proportion to that bond. A sybil operator can create many names, but each gains little influence unless the operator locks more capital behind it; spreading the same bond across jade, grove, and ridge accounts does not multiply its bidding power. The cost is capital tied up for the duration, plus losses if an agent breaks rules and its bond is slashed.
